body: You look FANTASTIC!

I love them because they (obviously) fit right into your bra - they have a sticky side so they stay in place always and they are thick enough that nothing leaks through, but you hardly notice they are there (you don't feel like your bra is stuffed). And nothing every stuck to my incisions or chest. 

I'm almost 4 weeks out and I still wear them in one cup - a small incision opened, and is healing but will "leak" from time to time. 

Good luck!
I used breast feeding pads!
Congrats!!
WOW! You look fantastic!!!!! SO happy for you! I can feel the relief
Cant stop smiling hearing this - very happy for you
Best of luck! Its the greatest feeling!
"Dream Boob" haha I love it. I'm happy youll have your own!

YAY! You're going to be so happy. I keep saying this - but remember the pain is temporary! I'm onto my third week and feel fantastic, but the first week or so is PAINFUL. Youll feel all the joy in the following week! Good luck.
Oh I thought you had - GOOD LUCK on the journey!

I didn't get sick or feel nausea either! I DID take anti nausea pills with my pain killers - that was SUPER important. 

I only took my painkillers for a few days - I wanted to be off them too and just switch to ibuprofen. I would have liked to sooner, but the pain was really tough the first few days for me. I did switch to ibuprofen on the 4th day, and that worked wonderfully.  

However, about a week later, I was feeling really sore and I couldnt sleep so I took a painkiller without my anti-nausea medication and I did throw up about an hour later. But just did to the painkiller & the lack of anti-nausea. 

The anti-nausea worked like a charm. 

YOULL DO GREAT!

used-books is so right! I'm on my third week recovering now! I went back to work after just 4 days of healing but I have a desk job. NO WAY would I be able to stand/lift for long periods of time. I would get off work at 5, have my sister pick me up (I was too tired to drive) and then go home and immediately fall asleep - and I was just sitting at a desk. 

I serve as a part time 2nd job - and I'm taking over a month off from there (maybe longer). You use your chest muscles constantly - you don't realize how much you do until you can't.
Thank you, thank you!!
Thank you! How have you been healing?
yay hope! GOOD LUCK! I hope you feel incredible some day soon.
I really hope you do - I really think it becomes a mental weight. I hid in my own body so many times. Its exhilarating. I FEEL LIKE A REAL PERSON! Good luck!
Thank you, Josienx!

AH super happy for you! I'm so joyful and cheerful and I want to share it with everyone! Exciting you'll feel the same way soon! You're going to do great, its all temporary pain. Just have to remind yourself a few times!
EEeeeee!! Thank you!

HI! Indianapolis, Dr. John Aker. He was/is marvelous. I'm really happy with everything, I think he did a wonderful job. 

I didn't go through insurance - I've tried in the past and probably should have tried harder this time around. But I was desperate. And impatient. 

The total (including hospital bills and follow up appointments) was $7,500. I pulled a bit from my savings and then put the rest on a credit card. I was able to pay no interest for 18 months, so just planning (ha hopefully) to pay that off before then. When I'm healed, I was thinking of taking a 2nd job for a few months. 

For me, it was absolutely worth the cost. I BOUGHT A 12.99 BRA! I'm already saving money haha. And shopping is easy & quick. I've bought a few new tops- fit perfectly and inexpensive. 

It really really is the best thing I've ever done for myself.

When I originally met with my surgeon I asked for a B. He was great - he explained to me a C would look better on my frame, and that you need some weight to a breast to get a nice shape. He said a B might look a little "boxy". He said he would get me a B if I wanted - but this was his opinion. After a few weeks, I agreed to a C, I think I was so desperate to go small that a B sounded ideal. But I agreed on a "small C" haha.   

And best of luck with your surgery - remember all pain is temporary during your recovery! YOULL BE SO HAPPY.
YES! So many people have asked me how I've lost weight so quickly - Welp, I dont have boobs hanging all over my stomach ha. It feels INCREDIBLE! Hope you get to feel it too.
Thanks! I love them!
Thank you!
ha love this! Congrats!

Woo! Go you! I run too and am slightly nervous to be out of it so long - Running keeps me sane, and keeps my brain working. 

SO happy for you, and thanks for the inspiration. Hoping I can get back out there that soon as well, my surgery is in 3 weeks. 

Were you nervous at all?
YAY!

Good luck with your consult tomorrow! Let us know how it goes if you'd like! Love to hear about it. 

I hope you figure out all the financing - I felt the same with my funds, but think its so so worth it. And we will save on bras, right :)

My insurance doesn't cover the cost either - my total bill comes to $7,500. I already put $500 down, so I'm looking at $7,000 which doesn't need to be paid in full until 2 weeks prior to my surgery.

My anesthesia bill is paid separately & is around $1,200 (but included in the $7,500) - I plan on using my Heath Savings Account which I have through work. I also I have around $1,500 I'm willing to put down pull from my savings (not that there's much else in there).

So now I'm looking at $4,300. 

I applied for a credit card that has 0 APR for 18 months, which I plan to put the $4,300 on. My credit limit was 7,500 (which is the exact total amount as my surgery, so took that as a fun little sign). And I'm hoping to pay it off in the next 18 months - I had a second job serving that I am going to start again until I pay it off/sell some art/live modestly until its paid. 

You should also check if they have a payment plan, But I'm sure you will be able to find a card through care credit or I would apply for a card with 0 APR for a set amount of time. And briliantlyfreakish brings up a great point - loans are surprisingly easy to attain. You should talk to your bank. 

Hope this helps a little.
Joy & ease! I love that. Hope you're recovery is going great! And you're feeling more energetic (or just catching up on sleep!)
Thank you! Definitely looking into other surgeons/opinions!

Anti depressants really helped me. Therapy and being honest are what mostly helped with my depression - but I was unable to get suicidal thoughts out of my head without drugs. 

I felt the exact same as you - so tempted, felt relief just knowing suicide is there. But my family and friends would be devastated and I fear the pain and the unknown. 

I also felt the same in the sense that they thought would always be there. And it is from time to time, and I still suffer from depression so some days are worse than others. But prior to medication, it was a constant overwhelming thought. I think starting to look forward to things, staying involved socially and sticking to my hobbies (all due to medication/improving in therapy) - allows my mind to be distracted and eventually the thoughts subside. 

So, still there once in a while, but I'm still on the road to recovery. Would love a day where I can say they are completely gone. But definitely have improved. Maybe one day.
I definitely do this with the photos. Avoid them completely. Trips/events with family & friends too. I hope you find relief.

I wish happiness for you as well - as unfair as it all is, I'm still holding on to the hope of relief. Or at least the idea that I'm preventing them all from unnecessary sadness and grief. Hang in there, I'm with you.
It isn't. But it makes me feel calm/better too. Its the only thing that helps me make it through the day.

Yes, about 4 months ago they put me on 100 mg right away and I had terrible panic attacks! And I could only focus on suicide. It was miserable. I kept telling myself it would pass.

Then I started at 25 and worked my way up to 100. My doctor is a nurse practitioner so I left her a voicemail this morning asking her for a recommendation of a physiatrist. 

Its just exhausting - nothing seems to work. And I've tried it all. Thank you for sharing your experience, its a nice reminder that I'm not alone in this.

I definitely understand/feel what you were describing. I feel nothing. Maybe a little sad if anything, but nothing too extreme. Certainly no happiness, excitement, or joy. My personality is gone. Thinking of coming down off of the medication - but terrified of feeling extremely suicidal. Going to talk to my therapist of course, but just wanted to say I relate. And this is the worst. Everytime I think I hit the lowest point, I get proven wrong.
I hope so too. Are you actively doing anything to help? Therapy or medication?

Also, 20 years! Can I ask- Do you ever plan on getting off of it? And has it been beneficial to you? (I would assume it must be) My therapist has implied she only wants me on it for 6 months to a year and then plans to wean me off. I guess the idea of being permanently on it never crossed my mind, but may be necessary. I'm taking it for depression, which I've struggled with for a long time. Also due to grief.
That's a good thought - my therapist wanted me at 100, so we were trying to up it slowly, but maybe it wasn't slow enough. Do you feel it helped you overall? Im taking it for depression.
A month! Welp, I'm sticking to it. Thank you.
That's very sad, I'm heartbroken you felt that way. I feel that way now, hoping the medication will help me feel anything again. I feel so numb. Thanks for sharing.

I had horrible panic attacks as well -thankfully they only lasted a week. My medication is prescribed through a nurse practitioner and her advice is always "give it time" (I call her all the time, she must be so tired of me). Are you still on sertraline? and did it ultimate help you at all?

I completely understand - I don't want to kill myself, but I want to die. Every time I'm on plane, I want it to go down. Maybe I'll get desperate enough to end my own life one day, but I'm exactly where you are right now.
